title: Derived sections over a w-contractible affine
statement:
Let $U$ and $\mathcal R$ be as in [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], and let $K$ be an arbitrary
(possibly unbounded) complex of $\mathcal R$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. Then the
natural map $K(U)\to R\Gamma(U,K)$ is an isomorphism in the derived category of
$\mathcal R(U)$-modules, where $K(U)$ is the complex of sections computed term by term. In
particular $H^q(U,F)=0$ for every sheaf of modules $F$ and every $q>0$.

proof.text: Work in the common universe and small skeleton of [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal R)$ and $\mathcal B=\Mod(\mathcal R(U))$, and write $E=\Gamma(U,-)$. The category $\mathcal B$ is abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives], used only for its abelian-category assertion. The ring sheaf need not be commutative. The small-site hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] apply in this universe, so $\mathcal A$ is Grothendieck abelian. Hence [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] gives a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective, even when $K$ is unbounded. Evaluation is additive: addition of module morphisms is sectionwise, and $E(f+g)=(f+g)_U=f_U+g_U=E(f)+E(g)$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: By [det-pe-wc-sections-exact], $E$ is exact. Here is the degreewise argument, with cohomology as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For any complex $C$, put $Z^n=\ker d_C^n$ and $B^n=\operatorname{im}d_C^{n-1}$. Apply $E$ to $0\to Z^n\to C^n\to B^{n+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^n\to Z^n\to H^n(C)\to0$. The first resulting exact sequence identifies $E(Z^n)$ with $\ker E(d_C^n)$; in the factorization $C^{n-1}\twoheadrightarrow B^n\hookrightarrow C^n$, the epimorphism and monomorphism remain such, so $E(B^n)=\operatorname{im}E(d_C^{n-1})$. The second resulting sequence therefore gives $H^n(E(C))\cong E(H^n(C))$. These identifications commute with maps of complexes because the maps on the kernels, images and quotients are induced by their degreewise components. In particular $H^n(E(s))$ corresponds to $E(H^n(s))$ and is invertible for every $n$. Thus $E(s):K(U)\to I(U)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This calculation uses only two adjacent differentials in each degree and imposes no boundedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), proof: expanded kernel/image calculation; blueprint proof, second sentence

proof.text: Use [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] for the additive functor $E$ and the K-injective resolutions from step 1; this defines $R\Gamma(U,-)=RE$ and its unit $\eta$. Write $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ for the localizations of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $I$ is K-injective, $\eta_I$ is invertible. Since $s$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $Q_{\mathcal A}(s)$ and therefore $RE(Q_{\mathcal A}(s))$ are invertible. The resolution comparison $c_s=\eta_I^{-1}\circ RE(Q_{\mathcal A}(s)):RE(Q_{\mathcal A}K)\to Q_{\mathcal B}(E(I))$ is consequently invertible. Naturality of $\eta$ gives $c_s\circ\eta_K=Q_{\mathcal B}(E(s))$. Step 2 and localization make the right-hand side invertible. Hence the specified natural map $\eta_K:Q_{\mathcal B}(K(U))\to R\Gamma(U,K)$ is invertible, not merely an abstract isomorphism between the two objects.

source.place: Tags 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies) and 070Y (lemma-K-injective-defined); blueprint proof, resolution computation and first conclusion

proof.text: Take $K=F[0]$. By the definition of cohomology and its factorization through localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $H^q(U,F)=H^q(R\Gamma(U,F[0]))\cong H^q(F(U)[0])$. For $q>0$, the term of $F(U)[0]$ in degree $q$ is zero, so its kernel and its cohomology quotient in that degree are zero. Thus $H^q(U,F)=0$.
